title: Confession and the Wall of Sin
english: In essence it is not light, but it is capable of receiving light. But its darkness is the passionate and desiring part.

If the mind is now enlightened by the Lord, sharing with it His own rays, the victorious movements and the irrational movements of the soul are enlightened through knowledge being perfectly accomplished; not that the irrational parts themselves participate in light (for they are incapable of knowledge), but that which is under an enlightened mind is guided by knowledge and virtue without needing a way. If the mind, which is said to be a lamp, is now enlightened by the Lord, then the darkness we have spoken of must necessarily follow being enlightened.

And this is what the Savior says: 'If the light in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!' (Luke 11:35). For if the eye of the body, that is, the mind, which ought to be a lamp, is deprived of light, then the other is much more so; in this way, the body of the soul becomes darkness, but it is not a human body, rather it is that which happens according to its irrational composition.

Perhaps also those enlightened in the knowledge of the truth have the lamp exhausted, the Lord having given this to them; and having performed actions rightly from the enlightenment of the mind, they have their darkness being enlightened. And this too should not be said of the basket. Those having possessed scientific contemplation concerning intelligible and invisible things have a lamp being enlightened by the Lord, but also regarding sensible things, being well-disposed according to opinion, they have the sense perceiving things luminously, which is darkness because it is not by itself capable of being enlightened, that is, receiving knowledge; for would the senses, even if they received knowledge, receive the irrational parts?

It is not otherwise possible to be saved from the surrounding bitter things by becoming in God; for someone becomes in God partaking of Him. Just as one having come to be in knowledge is saved from ignorances, so one hastening to be in God will be saved from temptation, not by not entering into temptation, but by not being caught by its snares.

For he who confesses Jesus before men is in him; for whoever confesses me before men, I will confess him before my Father who is in the heavens (Matt 10:32-33). For one partakes of him and confesses Jesus, and is confessed by God as being in him. But the multitude of things being done toward us irrationally separates us from God and discerns [a gap], as the prophet says: Is not the hand of the Lord able to save? Did his wrath grow because they did not listen? But your sins discern [a gap] between you and God. And he who now becomes in God, clinging to him and being toward him, surpasses the wall of sins by a little and casts them before and behind, so that, not being pierced through by anything, he may face God face to face.

Perhaps also the sense of bodily and sensible things, standing between our thought and God, separates us from him. But if we now, scientifically as much as possible, through the thought concerning God, grasp him above all bodies and senses, desiring to be united with him, we withdraw from the sensible and bodies as if to leap over the world and all visible things, so that we may be able to present ourselves to God. Our God is faultless in the way toward him (Ps 17:31). And this is virtue, through which, traveling by practice and discipline, we shall be shown faultless coming toward him. But especially faultless is the way of God, he who said: I am the way and the truth and the life (John 14:6). For through this way it is possible to come to the Father.

The word of the Lord, having been made fiery, is in the one who is truthful and pure, or is a fire that consumes the weakness of the matter of those partaking. He is a defender of all who hope in him. Those who know the weakness present to them, if they make those attacking them stronger, by casting hope upon God, are worthy to have him fight for them, saying, 'Fight, those who fight against me.' And thus God fights for them with his own shield, according to: His truth shall surround you with a shield (Ps 17:30). For no one is truly and principally God except the God of the Word, who is called the only-begotten God (Ps 17:32a).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Symbolic Interpretation of Psalm 17
english: Because he alone is as the Father God. For all the others are made gods by the presence of the Word of God. For those are gods by participation, toward whom the Word of God came. But the Savior, not possessing divinity, is God, a maker of gods.

In Psalm 17:32b (Εἰπὼν μηδένα θεὸν κυρίως ειναι πλὴν τοῦ κυρίου), having said that no god exists in the strict sense except the Lord, he says that no god exists in any way like our God. For none of those who are gods by participation can be like the Lord Jesus Christ, or like our God as the [one] of the only-begotten Father; for to us is God the Father and is Lord Jesus the Christ. And if even the two verses can be said to be parallel, he himself will understand.

In Psalm 17:33–34 (Ἐνταῦθα Περιζωννύων με δύναμιν λέγεται), 'He girded me with strength' is said. But according to Paul, the truth is that those having put on the armor of God are girded, from which it is gathered that the Christ is the power of God; for the Savior says, 'I am the truth' (Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀλήθεια), but Paul [says], 'Christ the power of God' (Χριστὸς θεοῦ δύναμις). And he set my way blameless, that is, he demonstrated. For to demonstrate now means to have demonstrated, just as [it is said] 'He has appointed him heir of all things' (Ον εθεκεν κληρονόμον πάντων). It is also good from this verse to proclaim the whole psalm from the person of Christ.

He who says these things, having refuted the serpent-like evils and the evil powers that worked them, has the feet of his own man prepared by God (that is, the walking powers), so that he may be able to say, 'I have run without lawlessness and have directed my course' (Ἀνευ ἀνομίας ἐδραμον καὶ κατηύθυνα); and having fulfilled the course, he will be heard in the high places by God: 'You yourself also stand with me' (Σὺ δὲ αὐτὸς στῆθι μετ' ἐμοῦ). And to stand in the high places is not something one has from himself, but from God.

In Psalm 17:35a (Ωσπερ τὰ ἄλλα καλά), just as other good things, so also we are taught by God to fight against the opposing powers. For he strikes the hands of the soul (I mean the active powers of it), and teaches how to skillfully hold the mental shield and the sword of the spirit and other spiritual defenses, and how one must use such things. For even the Savior, having become man, having fought on our behalf, taught us to overcome and to fight against the opposing power; and he says that stretching out his hands in prayer: 'I am surrounded by the difficulties...'

Remaining. 139 Symbolically, he set a bow called bronze upon the arms (Ps 17:35b); for because of the bronze, it represents the unpierceable or the strong, and because of the bow, the ability to release arrows from our own arms to wound those set against us.

140 Besides these, you have given to me a shield of salvation, having sent your Son to fight for me with his own shield (Ps 17:36). But also your discipline, he says, has perfected me to the end—that is, the disciplinary teaching and the strenuous training. He has brought me to the end, that is, unto a perfect resurrection and standing. For discipline signifies the disciplinary aspect, as in 'Take my discipline, do not let go' (Prov 3:11), but also the strenuous aspect through 'Do not despise the discipline of the Lord' (Prov 3:11). And thus, in both ways, your discipline has become a teacher of good things to me.

141 Having been aided by ten thousand through God, confidence arose to pursue the enemies; and the end of the pursuit is their falling to the end (Ps 17:38). For neither toil nor fear caused me to stumble.

142 Sparing those who were envenoming, he crushes them, so that they might become unshakeable and immovable in the enmity (Ps 17:39a). For, not intending to destroy them, he surrounds them with tribulation, so that, having perceived they are evil, they might cease from the intention of hatred.

143 The falling of the enemies under the feet of the holy one signifies nothing other than the submission of the various [kinds] (Ps 17:39b). For as it is trivial to stand in the hand of the law, the beginning of salvation is to fall from it. For one falling from it does not oppose it, but lies down and submits.

144 You caused all those rising up against me to stumble, not permitting them to advance in the face of evil (Ps 17:40b.41). For, being hindered from the impulse toward evil, they will fall down beneath me, regarding me as nothing other than their ruler and head, so that, instead of hating, they might become friends; for such are they whom you have destroyed; for you do not destroy their essence, but only that which has happened to them. For it is very fitting for the goodness of God to make the evil vanish, but not the essence of that which has happened to them.
145 For he says to some: 'And if you multiply the prayer, I will not listen to you' (Ps 17:42), because of your hands—that is, your deeds—which are murderous.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Recognition and Participation
english: And the eyes are full. Regarding those of whom the Word speaks, having become thickened by thinking of earthly and material things, bearing the image of the earthly, they are thinned through exhortations, admonitions, threats, and painful discipline, so that, as having become dust in the face of the Divine Spirit, which is called the tropical wind, all that is earthly, being dispersed by them by the breath of the Spirit, may become pure dust as their underlying substance, for whom it has happened to be earthly.

And if they also willingly follow this calling, the author says as if to a filthy city: 'Shake off your dust, Jerusalem' (Ps 17:43). But the Lord, or His imitator, the just, licks these even as mud in the streets. But this mud being licked will not be able to become an earthen vessel useful in the great house in which there are golden and silver and wooden and earthen vessels; but since the golden and silver are for honor and the wooden and earthen are for dishonor, the one cleansing himself from these becomes a vessel of honor, having been sanctified and made useful to the Master, prepared for every good work, while those who remain such mud in the streets—that is, the mire of pleasures and desires—are being freed from all roughness from the passions.

He who says these things, by instilling a uniformity through the licking, is now making them earthen vessels, if they should cleanse themselves by a spontaneous impulse as if to become vessels of honor, golden or silver. For just as some have become earthen vessels from golden and silver ones (For the precious sons of Zion, exalted with silver, how were they reckoned as earthen vessels of the work of hands? [Ps 51:7]), so from their own domestic choice they shall become golden or silver from earthen ones.

Regarding the second meaning of the name of knowledge, he shows both the knowing and the being known and being recognized by the one knowing the one being known. According to the former meaning, God knows all, and not only the diligent ones. For toward the lowly the Savior says: 'You justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts' (Mt 6:1); and in the prophet: 'Because I knew all your sins' (Ps 40:3). And according to the second [meaning]...

It is said that he recognizes only the righteous. For the Lord knew those who were his, but he ignored the wicked. The Savior says to them: 'Depart from me, workers of lawlessness, I never knew you' (Matt 7:23). And the people from the nations, not being known by the Savior, though he healed both demons and idols and practiced all manner of evil, having changed through repentance to serve Christ, came to him. And even the saying 'He did not know' is true. For it is not said: 'A people I do not know served me' (Matt 15:22). For he who is doing the works of wickedness is not known; but he who has ceased from sins was not known before, but is known now.

To this the apostolic word agrees, saying: 'But formerly, not knowing God, you served those which by nature are not gods; but now, having known God, and even more having been known by God' (Gal 4:8). For they did not know God, and they were unknown by him, but having known him, they were known by him. Perhaps it will seem to some that the spoken thing passes by: 'To the hearing of an ear I obeyed' (1 Sam 13:30), meaning to obey with an ear that obeys all things. But the ear is not intended to pass by or to be superfluous for the one obeying all things, so as to use a non-human and mortal hearing, but a divine ear added to the one approaching; for he added to me an ear for hearing.

'Alien sons have grown old' (Heb 1:6), and the following. God the Father, becoming the beginning and source of the good, becomes the source of those doing good works, and those who are found in doing what is necessary are truly sons of God, partakers of his only-begotten Son. But if those who did not draw near participate in the opposites (and these are the evils), they would be alienated from God, and the growing old would follow. For participating in virtue, in bright and imperishable wisdom and incorruption, they were finding constant renewal; but falling into wickedness, they would be growing old through their own corruption (if indeed it is so), being worn out.

And since the verse is about the Jews, they are not sitting by the oldness of the letter, nor are they falling by quantity, enduring the newness of the spirit, 'Alien sons and having grown old have become'; but they are also said to be double-minded and double-souled, reeling from their many tribulations. For to be double-minded...
